story:
Maria arrived at the airport at six in the morning. She had a big bag, a small backpack and a ticket to Peru. At the check-in desk, the woman asked for her passport. Maria looked in her bag, then in her backpack, then in her jacket. Nothing.
She called her brother. "Did I leave my passport at home?" she asked. He went to her apartment and looked on the table, in the kitchen and under the bed. Finally, he found it in the washing machine, inside her blue pants. It was dry, but a little wet in the corner.
He took a taxi to the airport and gave it to her forty minutes before the flight. Maria laughed, thanked him and promised to buy him a nice gift in Peru.

preguntas.q: Where was Maria at six in the morning?
Who looked for the passport in the apartment?
Where was the passport?
What did Maria promise her brother?

story:
Tom wanted to cook dinner for his parents and his grandparents. It was his first time. He went to the supermarket and bought fish, tomatoes, rice and a cake for dessert. He forgot the sugar, so he had to go back.
At home, he put the fish in the oven and started the salad. Then his phone rang. It was his friend Carlos. They talked about the football match for twenty minutes. When Tom went back to the kitchen, there was smoke everywhere. The fish was black.
His grandmother arrived first. She looked at the kitchen and smiled. "Don't worry," she said. "Let's order pizza." In the end, everyone ate pizza, salad and cake, and his grandfather said it was the best dinner of the year.

preguntas.q: Who was Tom cooking for?
Why did Tom go back to the supermarket?
What happened while Tom was talking on the phone?
What did the family eat for dinner?

story:
Laura started a new job at a bank last Monday. She was nervous, so she woke up very early and took the bus at seven. The bus was full and she had to stand for forty minutes.
Her boss, Mr. Brown, was tall and serious. He showed her the office, her desk and her new computer. "You need to learn this program this week," he said. Laura worked hard all day. At lunchtime, a woman named Sofia invited her to eat together. Sofia was funny and very friendly, and she explained a lot of things about the bank.
On Friday, Mr. Brown called Laura to his office. She thought it was a problem. But he smiled and said, "You did a great job this week." Laura took a taxi home to celebrate.

preguntas.q: Where does Laura work now?
How did Laura travel on her first day?
What was Sofia like?
Why did Mr. Brown call Laura on Friday?
opciones: To give her a new desk
To say she did a great job

story:
Ana's cousin was getting married on Saturday, and Ana didn't have anything to wear. On Thursday after work, she went to a clothes store downtown. She tried on a red dress, but it was too small. Then she tried a green one, but it was very expensive.
The salesperson was a young man with glasses. "What about this blue dress?" he asked. It was perfect and it was half-price. Ana also needed shoes. She found some black shoes, but they were not comfortable, so she bought brown ones.
When she got home, she showed everything to her husband. He looked at her and said, "It's beautiful, but our wedding invitation says the party is on the beach." Ana laughed. She had to go back to the store for sandals.

preguntas.q: Why did Ana go shopping?
What was the problem with the green dress?
What color were the shoes she bought?
Why did Ana need to go back to the store?
opciones: She needed sandals for the beach

story:
Peter and his kids planned a camping trip for the weekend. They packed a tent, sleeping bags, sandwiches and a lot of water. But on Saturday morning, it was raining hard and the radio said the rain would continue until Sunday night.
The kids were sad. "Can we go next weekend?" asked his daughter, Emma. Peter had an idea. He put the tent in the middle of the living room. They turned off the lights, used flashlights and told scary stories. His son, Leo, made a fire with red and yellow paper.
At night, they ate sandwiches inside the tent and watched a movie on the tablet. On Sunday, Emma said, "This was the best camping trip ever, and we didn't get wet!"

preguntas.q: What did Peter and his kids plan to do?
Why couldn't they go?
Where did they put the tent?
What did Leo make the fire with?

story:
Daniel had an important meeting in another city at ten o'clock. He arrived at the train station early, bought a coffee and got on the train on platform four. He sat by the window and started reading his notes.
After thirty minutes, a passenger next to him asked, "Are you going to the beach too?" Daniel looked out the window. He saw the sea. He was on the wrong train! He got off at the next station and called his boss. "I'm very sorry, I'm going to be late," he said.
His boss was not angry. "No problem," she said. "The meeting is online now. Do you have your laptop?" Daniel had it in his bag. He found a quiet café near the station and joined the meeting with a view of the sea.

preguntas.q: What time was Daniel's meeting?
What was Daniel doing on the train?
How did Daniel know he was on the wrong train?
Where did Daniel join the meeting from?
opciones: From a café near the station

story:
Sofia's grandmother was turning eighty on Sunday. The whole family wanted to surprise her. Sofia's mother made a chocolate cake, her uncle brought music, and the kids drew pictures for her.
The plan was simple: Sofia had to take her grandmother for a walk in the park while the others prepared the house. They walked slowly, talked about the old days and ate ice cream. Her grandmother said, "When I was young, I lived on this street and I rode my bicycle every day."
At five o'clock, they went back home. When they opened the door, everyone shouted "Surprise!" Her grandmother covered her face with her hands. Then she smiled and said, "I knew it. Your uncle can't keep a secret." Everyone laughed and they danced until late.

preguntas.q: How old was the grandmother turning?
What was Sofia's job in the plan?
opciones: To take her grandmother for a walk

preguntas.q: What did the grandmother do every day when she was young?
Why did the grandmother know about the party?
opciones: Her uncle can't keep a secret

story:
When Lucas moved to his new apartment, he didn't know anyone. The building was old and quiet. His neighbor across the hall was an older man who never said much. Every morning, he only said "Good morning" and walked away.
One night, there was no electricity in the whole building. Lucas didn't have candles or a flashlight. Then someone knocked on his door. It was his neighbor, with two candles and a hot cup of tea. "I thought you might need these," he said. His name was Mr. Wilson, and he was a retired music teacher.
They talked for hours in the dark. Mr. Wilson played the violin for him. Since then, every Friday, Lucas brings dinner and Mr. Wilson brings the music.

preguntas.q: How was the building where Lucas moved?
What happened one night?
What was Mr. Wilson's job before he retired?
What do they do every Friday now?

story:
Camila was thirty years old and she couldn't drive. Her friends always gave her rides, but she wanted to be independent. So she paid for ten driving lessons with an instructor named Joe.
The first lesson was terrible. She forgot to use the turn signal, she drove too slowly on the highway and she almost hit a trash can in the parking lot. Joe stayed calm. "Everyone makes mistakes at the beginning," he said.
Camila practiced every Saturday with her father in an empty parking lot. Little by little, she improved. Two months later, she took the driving test. She was nervous, but she did everything right. When the examiner said, "You passed," Camila called all her friends. "Now I can give you a ride!" she said.

preguntas.q: Why did Camila want to learn to drive?
What did Camila almost hit in the first lesson?
Who did she practice with on Saturdays?
What did Camila say to her friends at the end?
opciones: Now she could give them a ride

story:
On Monday morning, Javier dropped his phone in the street and the screen broke. He couldn't read his messages or call anyone. He was worried because he was waiting for an important email from a company.
At lunchtime, he went to a repair shop. The man said, "I can fix it, but it will take two days." Javier had to live without his phone. At first, it was difficult. He didn't know the time and he got lost on the way to the post office.
But then something changed. On the bus, he looked out the window instead of his screen. He read a book in the park and talked to an old friend he met by chance. On Wednesday, he got his phone back. The email was there: he got the job.

preguntas.q: What happened to Javier's phone?
How long did the repair take?
What did Javier do in the park?
opciones: He ate lunch with his boss

preguntas.q: What was in the email?
opciones: Good news: he got the job
